panels.rationale: Single intraoperative clinical photograph from an article on spontaneous postmenopausal urethral prolapse. The image shows the prolapsed urethral mucosa at the meatus, with four quadrant holding sutures and edematous/congested tissue, matching the in-text surgical description. The caption is empty, so age and ethnicity are not stated in caption or in-text mentions.
panels.attribution_text: Klein et al. Spontaneous postmenopausal urethral prolapse treated surgically and successfully.. Case reports in urology 2014. doi:10.1155/2014/695471. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
in_text_mentions: The mass was carefully dissected using four-quadrant excisional technique [8] (Figure 1). The patient was placed in the lithotomy position. Holding sutures were placed in the four quadrants of the prolapsing urethra. The edematous tissue was cut quadrant by quadrant, and in each one a mucosal to mucosal anastomosis was performed, before proceeding to the next quadrant. Traction on the holding sutures allowed good visualization of the proximal mucosa, and prevented its retraction towards the bladder. Once the tissue had been excised and repaired, cystoscopy was performed.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph from a case report of urethral prolapse in a young female child; shows the classic doughnut-shaped reddish congested mucosal mass encircling the urethral meatus, matching the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Awodele et al. A case report on urethral prolapse.. Oxford medical case reports 2025. doi:10.1093/omcr/omaf216. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Urethral prolapse presenting as a reddish, doughnut-shaped mass around the urethral meatus in a young female.
in_text_mentions: Due to concerns about possible sexual abuse, the parents contacted the school and police. A police officer accompanied them to the hospital for the evaluation. On examination, the child was calm, well-nourished, and hemodynamically stable. The systemic examination results were unremarkable. Genital examination revealed a reddish, doughnut-shaped, tender mass (2.0 × 1.5 cm) encircling the urethral meatus, which bled on contact. The hymen were intact with no signs of trauma or foreign bodies (Fig. 1).

panels.attribution_text: Jalloh et al. Urethral Prolapse Case Report: Surgical and Social Considerations in Senegal.. Case reports in urology 2022. doi:10.1155/2022/5541416. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Blood at the meatus of a urethral prolapse in a 7-year-old girl.
in_text_mentions: The first case is a 7-year-old female who was referred to gynecology for a second episode of vulvar bleeding. There was a suspicion for abuse noted by the gynecologist and referring physician. On examination, the patient had bleeding only at the urethral meatus, a circular bulging mass exceeding the limit of the meatus (Figure 1) and an intact hymen and vulva. She was diagnosed with urethral prolapse. After providing parental reassurance and education, the patient was managed surgically by excision and meatoplasty. She had no acute or chronic complications at 2-year follow-up.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Low-power H&E of the excised perimeatal prolapsing tissue in a male child with urethral prolapse, showing the polypoid keratinized stratified squamous mucosa with edematous stroma described in the caption; matches the histology finding of congested squamous mucosa with stromal edema. B: Higher-magnification H&E of the same urethral prolapse specimen showing keratinized stratified squamous epithelium with edematous, congested fibrovascular stroma, dilated veins and sparse lymphocytes, consistent with the prolapsed urethral mucosa of the target disease.
panels.attribution_text: Durakbaşa et al. A Very Unlikely Finding in a Male Child: Urethral Prolapse.. European journal of pediatric surgery reports 2017. doi:10.1055/s-0037-1604359. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Histopathologic examination of the specimen revealed ( A ) polypoid stratified squamous epithelium and edematous stroma (H&Ex10) and ( B ) stratified squamous epithelium and edematous fibrovascular stroma with dilated veins and a few lymphocytes in higher magnification (H&E x20). H&E, hematoxylin and eosin stain.
in_text_mentions: und examination of the upper and lower urinary tracts was normal. An orchiopexy operation as well as circumferential excision of the perimeatal prolapsing tissue with primary repair was done ( Fig. 2 ). The postoperative course was uneventful. The pathological examination of the specimen revealed keratinized stratified squamous epithelium, which is consistent with urethral mucosa ( Fig. 3 ). A uroflow study performed at the sixth postoperative week was normal with a maximal flow rate of 27 mL/s and an average flow rate of 13 mL/s. He is free of any complaints at the eighth postoperative month.

panels.rationale: Single clinical photograph of a child with a red-purple doughnut-shaped mass protruding at the urethral meatus, matching the captioned diagnosis of urethral prolapse and the article title describing an eight-year-old girl.
panels.attribution_text: Muteke et al. Urethral prolapse mimicking a uterine prolapse in an eight-year-old girl: A case report.. International journal of surgery case reports 2022. doi:10.1016/j.ijscr.2022.107169. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
